assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 physiology and its translation into incretin therapies for diabetes and obesity is an exceptional bench-to-bedside arc with very large clinical impact and clear conceptual originality in gut-islet-brain endocrine signaling.
assessment.attribution: Holst (physiology and secretion of GLP-1), Drucker (biology of GLP-1 and related peptides and the route to therapy) and Mojsov (identification of the active GLP-1 peptide and its insulinotropic form) form a coherent trio; Knudsen's industrial drug-design role is important but a three-person cap forces a choice. Mojsov's credit has been contested historically and my recollection of the details is not independently verified.
assessment.maturity: Multiple approved agents, large outcome trials and broad confirmation across diabetes, obesity and cardiovascular risk; recognition is timely and arguably pressing.
uncertainties: Allocation of credit between academic discoverers and the industry scientists who engineered long-acting analogues.
Disputed priority concerning the active GLP-1 peptide.
Long-term safety and durability of effect are still maturing.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Demonstrating that TNF is a dominant driver of chronic inflammation in rheumatoid arthritis and that blocking it is therapeutic transformed rheumatology and inflammatory disease management and established cytokine-targeted therapy as a paradigm.
assessment.attribution: Feldmann and Maini jointly led the mechanistic work on TNF in synovial cultures and the first clinical anti-TNF trials, a clean two-person configuration; others who identified or cloned TNF or engineered the antibodies are outside this credited set.
assessment.maturity: Three decades of clinical use, replicated across multiple autoimmune diseases and many agents, with stable interpretation and extensive real-world data.
uncertainties: Whether the committee views the work as clinical translation of earlier cytokine biology rather than a discovery in itself.
The precise relative contributions of TNF discoverers versus the clinical proof-of-concept investigators.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Engineering patient T cells with chimeric antigen receptors to obtain durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies is a landmark in cancer immunotherapy and cell therapy, with clear originality in receptor design and costimulation.
assessment.attribution: Sadelain (costimulatory CAR design and preclinical concept), June (first clinical successes in leukemia and CAR design for clinical use) and Rosenberg (adoptive cell therapy and early gene-engineered T-cell trials) are a plausible trio, though Eshhar and others who conceived the original chimeric receptor are not in the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Multiple approved products and long-term remissions, but late toxicities, secondary malignancies and limited efficacy in solid tumours remain open.
uncertainties: Credit for the original chimeric receptor concept is only partly captured by the supplied names.
Limited efficacy in solid tumours and long-term safety are not fully resolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Microbial rhodopsins used as genetically targeted light-gated tools gave neuroscience and physiology causal, millisecond control of defined cell types, an enormous methodological impact across the field.
assessment.attribution: Nagel and Hegemann identified and characterised channelrhodopsin function, and Deisseroth led its adaptation for neuronal control and circuit dissection; Boyden, Bamberg and Miesenböck are also decisive, so any three-person selection leaves a major unresolved allocation.
assessment.maturity: Widely replicated and adopted, with early clinical translation in vision restoration; recognition is timely though the toolset continues to evolve.
uncertainties: Six credited people with competing claims and a three-laureate limit.
Clinical translation is still early, so the case rests on research impact.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The unfolded protein response defined a new intracellular signaling pathway from the endoplasmic reticulum to the nucleus, with broad relevance to secretory-cell physiology, metabolic and neurodegenerative disease and cancer.
assessment.attribution: Walter and Mori independently and complementarily dissected the IRE1-HAC1/XBP1 mechanism and the pathway logic, which supports a fair two-person award.
assessment.maturity: Deeply confirmed mechanistically over decades; therapeutic translation (for example integrated stress response modulation) is still emerging, but the discovery is mature.
uncertainties: Direct disease-modifying clinical consequences are still being established.
Recognition of related contributions to the ER stress and integrated stress response field could be debated.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Notch is a core conserved cell-fate signaling mechanism with broad significance in development, stem-cell maintenance, immunity (including T-cell lineage decisions) and cancer.
assessment.attribution: Artavanis-Tsakonas (molecular characterization of Notch), Greenwald (genetic and mechanistic analysis in C. elegans) and Struhl (signaling mechanism and activation in Drosophila) are a reasonable trio, though other developmental geneticists also contributed, so I treat the exact allocation as uncertain.
assessment.maturity: Long established and confirmed across species; clinical relevance through Notch pathway in leukemia and developmental disease is real but therapeutic translation has been modest.
uncertainties: Many contributors in the Drosophila and C. elegans communities may need to be weighed.
Limited therapeutic translation relative to other candidates.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The cGAS-STING pathway explains how cytosolic DNA triggers innate immune and interferon responses, central to antiviral defence, autoimmunity (including interferonopathies and lupus-related biology) and cancer immunology.
assessment.attribution: Chen's identification of cGAS and cGAMP is decisive, while Barber and Ishikawa identified STING; Sun and Wu were co-discoverers in Chen's laboratory, so a three-person limit leaves some unresolved credit.
assessment.maturity: Mechanism is well confirmed and widely replicated, but therapeutic modulation is still in early clinical development and the pathway's full disease roles are being refined.
uncertainties: Therapeutic benefit is not yet established clinically.
Division of credit between the group leaders and the trainees in the Chen laboratory.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Virus-like particle HPV vaccines prevent persistent infection and cervical and other HPV-related cancers, with a very large and measurable public-health impact built on a clear conceptual innovation.
assessment.attribution: Lowy and Schiller (L1 VLP self-assembly and immunogenicity) and Frazer (VLP vaccine development with Zhou) are a plausible trio, though Jian Zhou's early contribution is not in the supplied credit and some priority questions are unsettled.
assessment.maturity: Population-level data show reductions in infection, precancer and now invasive cancer; strong confirmation, though the committee already recognised HPV in the 2008 prize for the causal virus discovery.
uncertainties: Priority and credit among several groups and institutions with patent-related disputes.
Possible view that vaccine development is applied relative to the earlier virology prize.
